### Part a


### Part b

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(broom)
library(mediation)

# Impute missing values
impute_data <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(is.na(.), median(., na.rm = TRUE), .))) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ ifelse(is.na(.), names(sort(table(.), decreasing = TRUE))[1], .)))
}

data_imputed <- impute_data(data)

# Variables to adjust for in the regression models
covariates <- c("Race_ethnicity", "Public.Asstce", "Use.Tob", "N.prev.preg", "Live.PTB", 
                "BL.GE", "BL..BOP", "BL..PD.4", "BL..CAL.3")

# Outcome variables
outcome_birthweight <- "Birthweight"
outcome_pregnancy_end <- "Preg.ended...37.wk"

# (b) Regression Adjustment for Causal Treatment Effect

# Regression model for Birthweight (with interactions)
birthweight_model <- lm(as.formula(paste(outcome_birthweight, "~ Group * (", 
                                         paste(covariates, collapse = " + "), ")")), data = data_imputed)
birthweight_summary <- tidy(birthweight_model) %>%
  mutate(
    conf.low = estimate - 1.96 * std.error,
    conf.high = estimate + 1.96 * std.error
  )
ate_birthweight <- birthweight_summary %>% filter(term == "GroupT") %>% 
  dplyr::select(estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

# Regression model for Pregnancy Ended Before 37 Weeks (main effects only)
pregnancy_end_model <- glm(as.formula(paste(outcome_pregnancy_end, "~ Group + ", 
                                            paste(covariates, collapse = " + "))), 
                           data = data_imputed, family = binomial)
pregnancy_end_summary <- tidy(pregnancy_end_model) %>%
  mutate(
    conf.low = estimate - 1.96 * std.error,
    conf.high = estimate + 1.96 * std.error
  )
ate_pregnancy_end <- pregnancy_end_summary %>% filter(term == "GroupT") %>% 
  dplyr::select(estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

# Print the ATE for Birthweight with formatted text output
cat("Estimated ATE for Birthweight:\n")
cat(" - Estimate:", ate_birthweight$estimate, "\n")
cat(" - Standard Error:", ate_birthweight$std.error, "\n")
cat(" - 95% Confidence Interval: (", ate_birthweight$conf.low, ", ", ate_birthweight$conf.high, ")\n\n")

# Print the ATE for Proportion of Pregnancies Ending Before 37 Weeks with formatted text output
cat("Estimated ATE for Proportion of Pregnancies Before 37 Weeks:\n")
cat(" - Estimate:", ate_pregnancy_end$estimate, "\n")
cat(" - Standard Error:", ate_pregnancy_end$std.error, "\n")
cat(" - 95% Confidence Interval: (", ate_pregnancy_end$conf.low, ", ", ate_pregnancy_end$conf.high, ")\n")


```

### Part c

```{r}
# (c) Fit Mediation Model (Mediator as the Outcome)
mediator <- "Change_in_BOP" # Define this variable as BL..BOP - V5..BOP
data_imputed <- data_imputed %>%
  mutate(Change_in_BOP = BL..BOP - V5..BOP)

# Specify only the desired variables for the mediator model
mediator_vars <- c("Group", "Change_in_BOP", covariates)

# Subset data to include only the mediator and specified covariates
mediator_data <- data_imputed %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(mediator_vars))

# Fit the mediator model using the subset data
mediator_model <- lm(Change_in_BOP ~ Group + ., data = mediator_data)

# Display a summary of the model to ensure it ran without errors
summary(mediator_model)

```

### Part d

```{r}
# (d) Outcome Model with Mediator as Covariate (including interaction with Treatment)
# Use mediator_covariates to ensure only the specified variables are included

# Construct the formula using the mediator_covariates list
mediation_formula <- as.formula(paste("Birthweight ~ Group * Change_in_BOP +", 
                                    paste(mediator_vars, collapse = " + ")))

# Fit the mediation model using the specified covariates
birthweight_mediation_model <- lm(mediation_formula, data = data_imputed)
birthweight_mediation_summary <- tidy(birthweight_mediation_model)

# Display the summary to check the results
summary(birthweight_mediation_model)

```

### Part e

```{r}
# (e) Estimate Controlled Direct Effect (CDE) and Natural Indirect Effect (NIE)
med <- mediate(mediator_model, birthweight_mediation_model, treat = "Group", mediator = "Change_in_BOP", boot = TRUE)

# Report CDE and NIE estimates and confidence intervals

# Extract CDE estimate and confidence interval
cde_estimate <- summary(med)$d.avg
cde_ci <- summary(med)$d.avg.ci

# Extract NIE estimate and confidence interval
nie_estimate <- summary(med)$z.avg
nie_ci <- summary(med)$z.avg.ci

# Print results with interpretations
cat("Controlled Direct Effect (CDE):\n")
cat("Estimate:", cde_estimate, "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: (", cde_ci[1], ",", cde_ci[2], ")\n\n")

cat("Natural Indirect Effect (NIE):\n")
cat("Estimate:", nie_estimate, "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: (", nie_ci[1], ",", nie_ci[2], ")\n")

```

## Problem 2

### Part a

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(randomForest)
library(dplyr)

# Read in the data
tico_data <- read.csv("tico_data.csv")

# Define the outcome variable and treatment indicator
outcome_var <- "hospital_free_28" # Number of hospital-free days over the first 28 days
treatment_var <- "corticobl" # Treatment indicator (corticosteroids)

# Ensure the treatment variable is a factor and remove missing values
tico_data <- tico_data %>%
  mutate(!!sym(treatment_var) := as.factor(!!sym(treatment_var))) %>%
  na.omit()

# Fit the Random Forest model with treatment interactions
model_rf <- randomForest(as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~", treatment_var, "+ .")),
                         data = tico_data, ntree = 500)

# Create modified data frames for treated and control scenarios
tico_data_treated <- tico_data %>%
  mutate(!!sym(treatment_var) := factor("1", levels = levels(tico_data[[treatment_var]])))

tico_data_control <- tico_data %>%
  mutate(!!sym(treatment_var) := factor("0", levels = levels(tico_data[[treatment_var]])))

# Predict outcomes under both treatment and control scenarios
predicted_treated <- predict(model_rf, newdata = tico_data_treated)
predicted_control <- predict(model_rf, newdata = tico_data_control)

# Determine the optimal treatment rule
optimal_treatment <- ifelse(predicted_treated > predicted_control, "1", "0")

# Add the optimal treatment rule to the original data
tico_data <- tico_data %>%
  mutate(optimal_treatment = optimal_treatment)

# Summarize the proportion who would benefit from treatment
treatment_benefit_proportion <- mean(optimal_treatment == "1")

cat("Proportion of patients who would benefit from treatment:", treatment_benefit_proportion, "\n")


```

The following function will output the optimal treatment decision for new data using the random forest model (model_rf) that was trained.

```{r,echo=TRUE}
optimal_treatment_rule <- function(new_patient_data) {
  # Predict outcome if treated
  treated_pred <- predict(model_rf, newdata = new_patient_data %>% 
                          mutate(!!sym(treatment_var) := factor("1", levels = levels(tico_data[[treatment_var]]))))
  
  # Predict outcome if not treated
  control_pred <- predict(model_rf, newdata = new_patient_data %>% 
                          mutate(!!sym(treatment_var) := factor("0", levels = levels(tico_data[[treatment_var]]))))
  
  # Return "1" if treatment prediction is greater, otherwise "0"
  return(ifelse(treated_pred > control_pred, "1", "0"))
}
```

### Part b

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(randomForest)

# Read in the TICO data
tico_data <- read.csv("tico_data.csv")

# Ensure 'corticobl' is a factor for treatment assignment
tico_data <- tico_data %>%
  mutate(corticobl = factor(corticobl))

# Subset data to focus only on 'ordpulmbl' (baseline oxygen support) and other necessary variables
data_subset <- tico_data %>%
  dplyr::select(hospital_free_28, corticobl, ordpulmbl)

# Step 1: Create virtual twins - predictions of outcomes if treated and if untreated
# Fit separate random forest models for treated and untreated groups

# Model for treated group
treated_model <- randomForest(hospital_free_28 ~ ordpulmbl, data = data_subset %>% filter(corticobl == 1))

# Model for untreated group
untreated_model <- randomForest(hospital_free_28 ~ ordpulmbl, data = data_subset %>% filter(corticobl == 0))

# Step 2: Generate predictions for both scenarios for all patients
# Predict outcomes if treated for all individuals
data_subset$pred_treated <- predict(treated_model, newdata = data_subset)

# Predict outcomes if untreated for all individuals
data_subset$pred_untreated <- predict(untreated_model, newdata = data_subset)

# Step 3: Calculate the treatment effect for each individual (predicted difference in outcomes)
data_subset <- data_subset %>%
  mutate(treatment_effect = pred_treated - pred_untreated)

# Step 4: Define the optimal treatment rule based on the sign of the treatment effect
# If the treatment effect is positive, treatment is beneficial; otherwise, it is not
optimal_treatment_rule <- function(baseline_oxygen_support) {
  prediction <- predict(treated_model, newdata = data.frame(ordpulmbl = baseline_oxygen_support)) -
    predict(untreated_model, newdata = data.frame(ordpulmbl = baseline_oxygen_support))
  ifelse(prediction > 0, "Treat with Corticosteroids", "Do Not Treat with Corticosteroids")
}

# Print summary of the proportion who would benefit from treatment
prop_benefit <- mean(data_subset$treatment_effect > 0)
cat("Proportion of patients who would benefit from treatment:", prop_benefit, "\n")

# Determine the threshold value for 'ordpulmbl' where treatment becomes beneficial
threshold_ordpulmbl <- data_subset %>%
  filter(treatment_effect > 0) %>%
  summarize(min_ordpulmbl = min(ordpulmbl)) %>%
  pull(min_ordpulmbl)

cat("Threshold value for baseline oxygen support (ordpulmbl) for beneficial treatment:", threshold_ordpulmbl, "\n")

```
